Actual `bridge-probe` Route is at `_registry.py:602-609` (handler `rebar._cli:_bridge_probe`, parser_factory `bridge_arms:build_probe`) — outside the cited 519-595 range.

`__init__.py:13` is the `reconcile routes to python -m rebar_reconciler` docstring bullet and `__init__.py:76-80` is `_reconcile()`, which the plan explicitly EXCLUDES; the actual bridge-probe handler `_bridge_probe` is at `__init__.py:105`. findings.finding: The Context line-range inventory that enumerates the alias patch sites (`_registry.py:415-450,519-595` and `__init__.py:13,76-80`) omits the `bridge-probe` registry Route and misattributes the `__init__.py` citation. The `bridge-probe` `Route(...)` block is at `_registry.py:602-609` (parser_factory `bridge_arms:build_probe`, handler `rebar._cli:_bridge_probe`), which lies OUTSIDE the cited `519-595` range. The cited `__init__.py:13,76-80` is the excluded `_reconcile` docstring bullet + function, not any of the five aliases' owners; the true handler/factory entries are at `_registry.py:423,429,451-452,458,606`. The inventory is a hand-authored line citation, not a symbol-reference-derived patch-site list, and it silently drops the bridge-probe route.
findings.location: Context / Problem: "Hidden CLI aliases remain in `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:415-450,519-595` and `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:13,76-80`"
scenarios: The `bridge-probe` Route at `_registry.py:602-609` is left in place because it is outside the cited line ranges — an unremoved alias, contradicting AC-1 ("Each of the five approved simple aliases is absent from the CLI registry").

An implementer following `__init__.py:13,76-80` edits (or is confused by) the excluded `_reconcile` code path instead of the five aliases, and never reaches the real bridge-probe handler wiring at `__init__.py:105` / `_registry.py:606`.
